title: Buddy Petit and Big Eye; Olympia band at the auditorium
summary: Buddy Petit played with her husband; Big Eye as a young player; the Olympia band was the first black band at the auditorium.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Well, what about Buddy Petit? What kind of trumpet player was he? Buddy Petit?
Did he play with your husband?

Oh, yeah, all of them. Buddy Petit was great, too. He was a good player. He had a funeral when he died. You know Armstrong came in, especially with him. He had a big funeral. Buddy Petit, oh, that was all... He was another fellow who drank hard, but he played. You could say he died young. And, oh, that was the boys really playing. They made money. All the boys made money. And I saw the boys in them days, I don't know, just... I think pick up that instrument. You know, they're self. They really are... I don't think there were a lot of them. Wasn't much like Reed as well. Like Bonnie, you know, Big Eye. Well, he was all right, too. But he started quite down. He was playing with Arnold and him. He was about 14 years old. He used to come practice home, you know. Roy's home. And then after he went away, you know. Arnold's... I think... Arnold was the first... The Olympia band was the first band ever played. Colored band played at the auditorium. Arnold, the Olympia band. I'm sorry, I couldn't hear you.
